items.title: Oocyte-specific OMC1 is required for maintaining chromosome cohesion through reproductive life
items.author: Kei-ichiro Ishiguro
items.content: Mammalian oocytes undergo prolonged meiotic arrest during which sister chromatids are linked by cohesin complexes. Cohesion deterioration during aging results in aneuploidy. Here, Iisaka, Yoshida et al. identify OMC1 as an oocyte-specific protein that preserves chromosome cohesion throughout reproductive life. The loss of OMC1 accelerates age-related aneuploidy.

items.title: Statins promote bone anabolism in estrogen deficiency by inducing osteogenic differentiation of skeletal stem/progenitor cells
items.author: Bo Shen
items.content: Yang et al. demonstrate that statins can compensate for reduced estrogen signaling in skeletal stem and progenitor cells, promoting bone anabolism during estrogen deficiency and suggesting therapeutic benefits beyond cholesterol management.

items.title: Uncovering the transcriptional hallmarks of endothelial cell aging via integrated single-cell analysis
items.author: Laura P. M. H. de Rooij
items.content: The Human Aging Endothelial Cell Atlas reveals how gene expression patterns of the human endothelium change with age, identifying reduced angiogenesis, altered mechanical signaling and a conserved gene program linked to endothelial senescence.

items.title: Type 2 immunity as a counter-regulatory axis in aging
items.author: Yi Zhang
items.content: Chronic low-grade inflammation is a hallmark of aging, but the endogenous programs that normally restrain it are far less understood than its drivers. Type 2 immunity is classically linked to allergy and anti-helminth defense, yet it also acts as a homeostatic circuit that preserves hematopoietic, macrophage and metabolic homeostasis. Here we argue that age-related erosion of this axis may contribute to inflammaging and represent a potential gerotherapeutic target for restoring immune homeostasis.

items.title: Chaperone-mediated autophagy curbs senescence
items.author: Matthew J. Yousefzadeh
items.content: Sereda and colleagues show that chaperone-mediated autophagy declines with aging, which leads to enhanced senescent cell burden that is driven, in part, by failed macrophage-mediated immunosurveillance that can promote tissue dysfunction and systemic aging.

items.title: Suppressing neural stem cell PLA2G7 restores inhibitory circuit function and improves cognition in aging mice
items.author: Nannan Guo
items.content: Wu, Wu and colleagues identify PLA2G7, a secreted lipid-metabolizing enzyme, as a negative regulator of inhibitory synapses in the dentate gyrus. Suppression of PLA2G7 in neural stem cells enhances synaptic transmission and cognitive performance in aged mice.

items.title: Transcriptomic reprogramming screen identifies SRSF1 as a regulator of aging
items.author: George M. Church
items.content: Plesa, Jung and colleagues conduct an in vitro transcriptomic reprogramming screen and identify splicing factor SRSF1 as capable of reducing transcriptomic age without loss of cell identity; they then implicate SRSF1 as a regulator of aging in worms and mice.

items.title: Senescent-like activated naive B cells contribute to progression to clinical rheumatoid arthritis
items.author: William H. Robinson
items.content: Applying single-cell multiomics to people at risk of rheumatoid arthritis, Wu, Zhang, Moon and colleagues identify an expansion of activated, senescent-like B cells associated with disease development. These cells express poly- and autoreactive antibodies and present self-antigens to T cells.
